item.title: China to launch climate leadership program
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China will launch the first project under a leadership program that aims to cultivate leading climate talents for other developing countries in 2027, as the country continues to strengthen South-South cooperation on climate change and support developing nations in improving their climate governance capacity. The announcement was made on Wednesday at the 14th High-level Forum on South-South Cooperation on Climate Change, held at the COP31 China Pavilion. Officially known as the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, COP31 opened on Monday and will run through Nov 20. The program is a flagship initiative led and initiated by China and implemented in cooperation with diverse international organizations, institutions, enterprises and universities to cultivate leading talents for other developing countries in formulating domestic climate governance policies and possessing a strong understanding of international coordination and cooperation, according to a media release from the Ministry of Ecology and Environment. The ministry highlighted an open and diverse partner network as a prominent feature of the program. At present, the United Nations Environment Programme, United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, the World Meteorological Organization, the International Renewable Energy Agency, Global Energy Interconnection Development and Cooperation Organization, Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD and Chinese tech giants Xiaomi, Tencent and Lenovo have confirmed their participation in the partner network, the release said. The forum also introduced the "China South-South school on climate change" capacity-building system, a multilevel and wide-ranging capacity-building program for countries of the Global South. Based on China's experience in climate action and green, low-carbon and high-quality development, the school will provide training and policy exchanges in areas including climate mitigation, adaptation, carbon market mechanisms and climate finance, according to the ministry. It said the South-South school will also organize field visits to help participants gain firsthand experience of China's green and climate-resilient development practices. Addressing the event, Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng said countries of the Global South are bound by a shared future, and only through solidarity and cooperation can they achieve green development. He called on members in the Global South to join hands to advance green development and work together to protect our planet, strengthen climate resilience and build a robust disaster prevention and mitigation network, as well as to beef up capacity building and lay a solid foundation for long-term climate action. China will continue to uphold the concept of a community with a shared future for humanity, deepen South-South climate cooperation, and jointly write a new chapter of sustainable development for the Global South, Han said. Huang Runqiu, China's minister of ecology and environment, said climate change is a common challenge facing all humanity and is closely linked to global sustainable development, security and prosperity. As a member of the Global South, China will continue to support other developing countries within its capacity, share opportunities for low-carbon development, build climate-resilient communities and promote a clean, beautiful and prosperous future for the Global South, he added. More than 250 representatives from China, Comoros, Antigua and Barbuda, Nigeria, Zambia and Ethiopia, as well as the UN, UNFCCC secretariat, WMO, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition and IRENA attended the forum, according to the ministry.

item.title: Decks cleared for Jupiter mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
The China National Space Administration has begun to take concrete steps to prepare for one of its ambitious interplanetary expeditions — the Tianwen 4 that aims to explore the Jovian system. The administration announced on Friday that the robotic probe is set to orbit Jupiter and land on its second-largest moon, Callisto, for close observation and survey. To achieve these goals, the CNSA's Lunar Exploration and Space Engineering Center started soliciting research and development proposals on Friday for scientific equipment that mission planners have decided to put on the Tianwen 4 spacecraft. According to the center, the Tianwen 4 will be equipped with 12 scientific payloads on its orbiter and lander. The orbiter will carry 10 payloads for two core research areas. Space environment detection tools — including a magnetic field and wave detector, particle analyzers, a soft X-ray spectrometer and a far-ultraviolet imager — will explore Jupiter's multiband auroras, the interaction between its vast magnetosphere and solar wind, and how solar particles spread through the outer solar system. Remote sensing apparatuses such as cameras, a laser altimeter, a visible-infrared imaging spectrometer and a gamma-ray spectrometer will map Callisto's terrain, analyze its surface composition and detect radioactive elements. The Callisto-bound lander will bring two in-situ measurement instruments — a surface composition analyzer will identify materials at the landing site via Raman spectroscopy, while the other, a surface magnetometer, will take on-site magnetic readings. Combined with orbital data, the surface magnetometer will help separate ionospheric and interior magnetic signals, offering key insights into Callisto's internal structure and its potential subsurface ocean. The center noted that it encourages overseas institutes to join programs led by Chinese organizations, or submit their own proposals. According to information previously published by Chinese space mission planners, the Tianwen 4 probe is scheduled to be launched by a Long March 5 heavy-lift carrier rocket from the Wenchang Space Launch Center in Hainan province around 2029. To date, humankind still lacks comprehensive knowledge of the Jovian system and has performed only a handful of exploration operations. Therefore, the gas giant planet is full of opportunities for science and discovery, according to Zhang Rongqiao, a top mission planner at the CNSA. While Jupiter, the largest planet of our solar system, has been known since ancient times, the first detailed observations of it were made by Galileo Galilei in 1610 with a small telescope. The first spacecraft to visit Jupiter was the United States' Pioneer 10 in 1973. Since then, this planet has been visited by several passing probes and orbiters. The most recent Jovian mission was launched by NASA in October 2024. The spacecraft, named Europa Clipper, is the first mission designed to conduct a detailed study of Jupiter's icy moon Europa. The spacecraft is traveling 2.9 billion kilometers to reach Jupiter in April 2030.

item.title: What makes international students want to stay in Beijing?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
They came to study. What makes them want to stay? From professional ambitions and everyday acts of kindness to a young Brazilian's journey from student to entrepreneur, discover their stories of building a future in Beijing.

item.title: Xi to attend APEC events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, next week, with the high-profile gathering expected to chart the course for stronger Asia-Pacific cooperation at a time of rising global uncertainty. He is also scheduled to attend the opening ceremony of the APEC CEO Summit 2026 and deliver a keynote speech. On the sidelines of the APEC gathering, he will host a welcoming banquet for participating leaders and representatives, as well as hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders, according to the Foreign Ministry. Since taking office as president in 2013, Xi has attended or chaired all APEC economic leaders' meetings, putting forward a series of pragmatic proposals and initiatives. The upcoming meeting in Shenzhen, which is themed "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", marks China's third time hosting APEC, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. China has designated openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priorities for APEC China Year, hosting more than 300 related events, including ministerial meetings on trade, finance and energy, over the past year. More than 10,000 representatives have participated in these events and reached a series of common understandings on cooperation, laying a solid foundation for the high-level gathering in Shenzhen, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said on Friday at a regular news conference in Beijing. "We look forward to building further consensus and agreeing on the APEC Shenzhen Leaders' Declaration among all member economies, as well as more practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, the digital economy, artificial intelligence and so on, to inject strong impetus into the prosperity and growth of the Asia-Pacific and the world," Mao said. Founded in 1989, APEC is a premier economic cooperation platform in the Asia-Pacific region, bringing together 21 member economies that account for nearly 40 percent of the global population, around 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of world trade. Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the APEC Secretariat, said at a media briefing in Singapore earlier this month that APEC brings its 21 economies together "to share experiences, assess different policy approaches and identify areas where further progress is needed". Australian economist Peter Drysdale said the Asia-Pacific community should be a beacon for the world, adding that projecting common interests through APEC and building on its founding principles are important not only for the region but also for the rest of the world. APEC is a stabilizing force in the international political economy, Drysdale told Xinhua News Agency in a recent interview. "It provides a set of principles that are going to be absolutely fundamental to managing the difficulties we have in the world today," he said, noting that it "reduces the uncertainties in the world, creates more certainty". Foreign Minister Wang Yi said that amid the fluid international landscape, the Asia-Pacific has remained a zone of stability, an engine of growth and a high ground for cooperation. At the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting held earlier this month, he said that the upcoming leaders' meeting is "an important event bearing on the future development of the Asia-Pacific". The APEC CEO Summit, scheduled to run alongside the leaders' meeting, has attracted strong global interest, with government, business and media participants expected to exceed 2,000, according to the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, organizer of the two-day event. Business representatives from all 21 APEC economies have registered to participate, with the United States accounting for the largest number of corporate participants among APEC economies other than China. The event has also attracted reputable companies from non-APEC members, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Switzerland. "This shows that, in an uncertain world, China is the greatest source of certainty," CCPIT spokeswoman Wang Wenshuai said late last month when briefing reporters on preparatory work for the event. Data from the General Administration of Customs shows that China's trade with other APEC economies reached 27.08 trillion yuan ($4 trillion) in the first 10 months of 2026, up 25.4 percent year-on-year.

item.title: Museum expo aims to strengthen intl exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
The 11th Chinese Exposition of Museums and Relevant Products and Technologies opened on Friday in the coastal city of Haikou, capital of Hainan province, with Egypt serving as the expo's first-ever country of honor — a move that experts said signals a broader push to strengthen international museum exchanges. As the largest and most influential expo in China's museum sector, the event has been held biennially since 2004. This year, it brings together almost 600 museums and around 200 cultural heritage-related enterprises in Haikou, showcasing cutting-edge advances in the protection of cultural relics, digital museums, exhibition display technology and cultural creative products. The theme this year is "Museums for High-Quality Development: Empowering with Technology, Connecting with the Future". The four-day event features 12 thematic areas, including achievements in museum development, digital and intelligent technologies, international exhibitors, non-State-owned museums and cultural heritage corporations. The expo introduced a country-of-honor mechanism, with Egypt serving in this capacity. Three major Egyptian cultural institutions — the Grand Egyptian Museum, the Egyptian Museum in Cairo and the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization — are taking part in the international exhibitors' area. French institutions, including Universcience — Cite des Sciences et de l'Industrie in Paris, are also exhibiting. Guan Qiang, president of the Chinese Museums Association, said that while the expo had previously hosted foreign museums, no participating nation had been given the status of a country of honor. By introducing this format, the organizers hope to strengthen future exchanges with the museum sectors of other countries.

item.title: What APEC has to do with your fruit plate
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
It's November, and Chilean cherries continue to arrive in China. In 2008, Chilean cherries were officially granted zero-tariff access to the Chinese market. Once a luxury item, they now reach Chinese dinner tables at lower prices and in fresher condition, thanks to direct maritime routes, streamlined logistics, and faster customs clearance. The cherry trade not only enriches Chinese dinner tables — it also sustains Chilean livelihoods. This is something the APEC has been doing for more than 30 years — advancing free and open trade and investment in the Asia-Pacific. Watch the video to see what APEC has to do with ordinary people like us.

item.title: Former UNESCO chief: High expectations for APEC Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov 18 to 19. Irina Bokova, former director-general of UNESCO, told China Daily that Shenzhen's transformation from a fishing village into a bustling metropolis with universities, technology, culture, economy, and finance is remarkable. As a green city and a city of learning, Shenzhen exemplifies China's inclusive development. Amid global turbulence, Bokova hopes this APEC meeting will foster dialogue, dispel mistrust and bring economies together to tackle world challenges. Watch the video!

item.title: Asia-Pacific needs digital bridges, not 'digital fences'
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
During an interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Ong Tee Keat, president of the Belt and Road Initiative Caucus for Asia Pacific in Malaysia, stresses inclusive digital supply chain finance, local-currency settlement and inclusive credit — rejecting "small yards and high fences"— plus capacity building so the digital dividend leaves no one behind. During the interview, Ong says China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 putting digital trade and sustainable innovation at the core of regional integration. More supportive measures will release a great regional market potential. Ong adds that interoperable digital frameworks let small traders access regional value chains through QR payments, e-commerce and paperless customs. But compliance burdens and tech disruption can marginalize grassroots entrepreneurs and uneven digital readiness makes coordination hard. Therefore, the region needs more coordinative efforts to solve the problems. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Pan Yixuan)

item.title: Mutual respect key to cooperation, says ex-ambassador
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Mutual respect and multilateralism are essential to managing international differences and strengthening cooperation, former Chinese ambassador to France Kong Quan said on Wednesday at the Paris Peace Forum, stressing that China's development offers opportunities rather than threats to other countries. Speaking at a session titled "Making Sense of China's Global Role and Impact", Kong, who is also a standing member of the China Economic and Social Council, said countries should recognize their differences in political systems and stages of development while seeking common ground through dialogue. "The diversity of the world is what makes humanity beautiful," he said. "China has never asked any country to embrace all its policies. What we want is to be understood on the basis of China's realities, in all their complexity and diversity." Kong identified mutual respect as one of four principles guiding China's approach to international relations, alongside responsibility, multilateralism and cooperation based on respect for sovereignty. Regarding multilateralism, Kong said China supports making international governance fairer and more equitable rather than establishing exclusive blocs. Global South countries remain underrepresented in international affairs despite their growing importance, he said. "The goal is neither to replace the United Nations nor to ask countries to choose sides, but to give more countries the opportunity to participate in discussing international rules and sharing the benefits of development," he said, referring to China's support for BRICS and other South-South cooperation mechanisms. Mauricio Favero, head of the Special Office for Diplomatic Planning at Brazil's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said multipolarity must be accompanied by multilateralism. "Multilateralism anchored in dialogue, negotiation and peaceful coexistence is basic," he said, adding that the challenges facing humanity demand a collective action. Kong said national sovereignty and international cooperation are not mutually exclusive. "China respects the sovereignty of all countries, as well as their legitimate security concerns," he said. Addressing emerging challenges in AI, data governance and critical technologies, Kong called for distinguishing genuine security risks from generalized and politicized security anxieties. "We support a greater role for open-source communities and open standards, which can make innovation more transparent, more inclusive and less monopolized by a minority," he said. Kong also called for strengthening technological capabilities in developing countries to prevent them from being marginalized in the latest wave of technological transformation. Concluding his remarks, Kong said China is not and will never be a danger to anyone, but an opportunity for development and cooperation. "It is not a rival, still less an adversary, as some claim, but rather a reliable partner," he said, noting that China remains consistent in its strategy and actions. zhangzhouxiang@chinadaily.com.cn
